The help screen ('* 포스트박스 사용해보셨나요? * · 24시간 어디서나 택배 접수 가능') includes five tiles: '운송장 롤 교체' (Replace waybill roll), '편의점 택배란?' (What is convenience store parcel?), '운임안내' (Rates), '접수불가 품목' (Prohibited items), and '포장방법' (Packing method).
The entire interface observed is in Korean only, with no visible language switcher on the main or sub-screens; a visible desktop mouse cursor arrow appears on screen after taps.
interpretation: Exposing both '현장 접수' (walk-in) and '예약 접수' (app pre-booking) shows how phone pre-entry reduces typing time on a shared public kiosk while keeping walk-in drop-off possible.
Confirming '국제택배' directly on the walk-in screen partially answers the open question from observation 013 about international shipping availability at emart24 kiosks.
Placing '운송장 롤 교체' (waybill roll replacement) directly in the public help menu suggests either staff or experienced users rely on the same touchscreen interface for basic consumable maintenance.
open: Which international courier partner handles '국제택배' from emart24, and does it require filling customs forms on the kiosk or in advance on mobile?
After weighing and printing a waybill on this kiosk, is payment completed at the main convenience store register?

observations.title: Gumeonggage Ajeossi unmanned snack kiosk, Post-it wall and smart alcohol fridge
observations.subject: gumeonggage-ajeossi
observations.scenario: Entering a compact unstaffed snack, toy and ice-cream store, viewing its card-only kiosk surrounded by handwritten Post-it notes and an automated alcohol fridge, and tapping through the Order Queen checkout interface.

requires: Card, Kakao Pay, Naver Pay, PAYCO, or manual bank transfer
unverified: Which Korean ID or mobile authentication method unlocks the '신선한 술 냉장고' alcohol refrigerator, and whether foreign residents or visitors can pass its verification
Whether foreign-issued cards work on the Order Queen kiosk terminal

media.caption: Unmanned checkout station with '카드전용' (Card only) sign, 24-hour CCTV notice, yellow bank-transfer and help-phone stickers (account details and mobile numbers blurred), wall of customer Post-it notes, insulated bags, and plush bear.
Store interior showing an unattended age-verification alcohol refrigerator ('신선한 술 냉장고 / 인생 술장고', '한번 인증하면 평생 자동인증') alongside toys, snacks, and an overhead CCTV dome camera.

Kiosk welcome screen featuring the '구멍가게 아저씨' mascot, red '시작하기 Start' button, Kakao Pay and Naver Pay stickers, and top bank-transfer/support stickers (account number, holder name, and mobile number blurred).
Order Queen scanning screen with quick-pick bag tiles ('큰봉투(1장) 100원', '보냉백 600원') using generic cutlery icons above a two-step barcode scan and payment prompt (top stickers blurred).
Cart list after selecting the barcode-less insulated bag ('#1 보냉백 · 수량 1개 · 주문 금액 600원') with illuminated barcode scanner and '결제하기' CTA (top stickers blurred).

observed: The yellow-themed self-checkout kiosk sits beneath a bold '카드전용' ('Card only') sign and a wall covered in dozens of handwritten customer Post-it notes and drawings.

Above '카드전용', a printed store notice states: '24시간 cctv 녹화중입니다.' (24-hour CCTV recording), '파손·절도 발생시 신고 및 손해배상 청구합니다.' (damage or theft will be reported with damages claimed), asks visitors to return baskets and cancelled items, and lists a mobile inquiry number (blurred).

Two yellow stickers taped across the top bezel of the kiosk provide a '계좌이체' (bank transfer) account at Hana Bank with account number and holder name (blurred), plus a '사용방법을 모르거나 도움이 필요하실 때' ('If you don't know how to use it or need help') mobile number (blurred).

Payment hardware below the screen carries stickers for '카카오페이 됩니다 (Kakao Pay)', 'N pay', and 'PAYCO', alongside a thermal receipt slot ('영수증을 잡아당기지 마세요' — do not pull the receipt), an optical barcode scanner window, and a card slot.

Inside the store, a yellow-framed alcohol refrigerator labeled '신선한 술 냉장고 / 인생 술장고' ('Fresh alcohol fridge / Life alcohol fridge') has a locked glass door with an embedded verification tablet and sign reading '한번 인증하면 평생 자동인증' ('Verify once, automatic verification for life').
The kiosk runs 'Order Queen' ('오더퀸 솔루션') software: an idle screen displays the '구멍가게 아저씨' mascot and a bilingual red CTA ('시작하기 / Start').

Tapping Start opens a two-part screen: the upper half shows two quick-pick buttons for items without barcodes—'큰봉투(1장) 100원' (large bag, ₩100) and '보냉백 600원' (insulated bag, ₩600)—both using generic restaurant plate-and-cutlery icons; the lower orange panel gives two numbered instructions ('1. 상품 바코드를 스캔하세요. / 2. 하단의 원하는 결제방식을 선택하여 결제해주세요!').

Tapping '보냉백' replaces the orange prompt with a cart table ('선택하신 주문내역: #1 보냉백 · 수량 1개 · 주문 금액 600원'), activates the red optical barcode scanner light below the screen, and exposes '주문취소' (Cancel order) and '결제하기' (Pay).
interpretation: Like zero STORE (019), this unstaffed shop layers informal human workarounds—handwritten Post-it notes, a plush bear, a Hana Bank transfer fallback, and a mobile help number—directly onto a strict '카드전용' + 24-hour CCTV self-checkout kiosk.
The generic fork-plate-spoon icons on '큰봉투' and '보냉백' suggest off-the-shelf restaurant kiosk software (Order Queen) repurposed for unmanned retail without custom retail iconography.

Whereas staffed convenience stores like emart24 (001) halt self-checkout and hand alcohol purchases to a cashier, this fully unstaffed shop replaces staff age checks with an automated verification refrigerator ('인생 술장고').
open: What exact authentication method (PASS app, resident registration number, mobile ID, or card) does '인생 술장고' use to verify age once and auto-verify thereafter, and is it accessible to foreign residents?
Why do unmanned shops post '카드전용' ('Card only') prominently while simultaneously taping a bank-transfer account directly onto the kiosk bezel?
How often do owners read or moderate the customer Post-it wall?
